read_protocol: abstract + method/system + conclusion + limitations/future-work; primary paper or author preprint only

hypotheses.I6: public run ledger and external experiment control plane

papers.title: Multi-Task Identification of Entities, Relations, and Coreference for Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction
papers.gap: Abstract-level fixed-schema extraction does not model evidence sufficiency, admission state, or cross-paper conflict.

papers.title: A General Framework for Information Extraction using Dynamic Span Graphs
papers.gap: Dynamic span graphs remain task-local; confidence is not calibrated as a graph-admission probability and provenance is not a first-class state.

papers.title: Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction with Contextualized Span Representations
papers.gap: Contextual spans improve extraction but do not decide whether the supporting text is sufficient for a scientific assertion.

papers.title: SciREX: A Challenge Dataset for Document-Level Information Extraction
papers.gap: Document-level n-ary relations expose a large human-model gap; versioned cross-paper evidence and contradiction states are outside scope.

papers.title: A Joint Neural Model for Information Extraction with Global Features
papers.gap: Sentence-level global decoding optimizes extraction consistency, not document provenance, evidence completeness, or calibrated abstention.

papers.title: Structured Prediction as Translation between Augmented Natural Languages
papers.gap: Generative serialization unifies tasks but can produce structurally plausible unsupported outputs without a hard evidence contract.

papers.title: Text2Event: Controllable Sequence-to-Structure Generation for End-to-end Event Extraction
papers.gap: Constrained decoding targets event schemas, not cross-document relation verification or evidence-state transitions.

papers.title: A Frustratingly Easy Approach for Entity and Relation Extraction
papers.gap: The strong pipeline baseline still propagates entity errors and does not preserve evidence lineage through relation acceptance.

papers.title: Packed Levitated Marker for Entity and Relation Extraction
papers.gap: Marker-based gains depend on supervised fixed schemas and do not address full-paper provenance or temporal contradictions.

papers.title: Unified Structure Generation for Universal Information Extraction
papers.gap: Universal structure generation improves transfer, but generated records are not guarded by evidence sufficiency and selective admission.

papers.title: DEGREE: A Data-Efficient Generative Event Extraction Model
papers.gap: Definition-guided generation is data-efficient but event-centric, schema-dependent, and lacks evidence-linked adjudication.

papers.title: ReSel: N-ary Relation Extraction from Scientific Text and Tables by Learning to Retrieve and Select
papers.gap: Text-table evidence selection remains domain/task bounded and does not expose multi-agent disagreement or calibrated graph states.

papers.title: GLiNER: Generalist Model for Named Entity Recognition using Bidirectional Transformer
papers.gap: Open-label NER stops before canonicalization, relation verification, and evidence-backed graph admission.

papers.title: SciER: An Entity and Relation Extraction Dataset for Datasets, Methods, and Tasks in Scientific Documents
papers.gap: The benchmark improves scientific coverage but remains small and does not evaluate temporal conflict or downstream decision calibration.

papers.title: GLiREL: Generalist Model for Zero-Shot Relation Extraction
papers.gap: Zero-shot relation typing depends on candidate spans and does not itself prove evidence sufficiency or provide calibrated abstention.

papers.title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
papers.gap: Wikipedia claims and sentence evidence do not capture scientific modality, full-document context, or evolving conclusions.

papers.title: MultiFC: A Real-World Multi-Domain Dataset for Evidence-Based Fact Checking of Claims
papers.gap: Heterogeneous labels and source formats complicate uniform evidence-span supervision and calibrated cross-domain decisions.

papers.title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
papers.gap: SciFact is abstract-based and small; full-paper, cross-paper, temporal, and graph-admission decisions remain open.

papers.title: HoVer: A Dataset for Many-Hop Fact Extraction and Claim Verification
papers.gap: Curated Wikipedia hops do not represent open scientific evidence completeness or source disagreement.

papers.title: Get Your Vitamin C! Robust Fact Verification with Contrastive Evidence
papers.gap: Synthetic contrastive edits improve robustness but underrepresent scientific semantic strength, modality, and real source conflict.

papers.title: Improving Scientific Claim Verification with Weak Supervision and Full-Document Context
papers.gap: Full-document verification still yields a claim label rather than a versioned evidence object with calibrated admission state.

papers.title: FAVIQ: FAct Verification from Information-seeking Questions
papers.gap: Ambiguous QA exposes retrieval ambiguity but not scientific provenance, relation state transitions, or temporal conflict.

papers.title: Fact-Checking Complex Claims with Program-Guided Reasoning
papers.gap: Program decomposition inherits parser and retrieval errors; evidence sufficiency and uncertainty are not independently calibrated.

papers.title: RARR: Researching and Revising What Language Models Say, Using Language Models
papers.gap: Research-and-revise can attach weak or irrelevant sources and lacks a structured independent admission gate.

papers.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
papers.gap: Atomic scoring depends on automated decomposition and retrieval; it is an evaluator, not a persistent evidence-state model.

papers.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
papers.gap: Self-consistency measures disagreement, not truth, and correlated samples can confidently reproduce the same error.

papers.title: AVeriTeC: A Dataset for Real-world Claim Verification with Evidence from the Web
papers.gap: Web evidence is mutable and noisy; dataset labels do not provide scientific KG admission or temporal supersession semantics.

papers.title: FacTool: Factuality Detection in Generative AI -- A Tool Augmented Framework for Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Scenarios
papers.gap: Tool reliability and API drift enter the verifier, while calibrated abstention and run-level provenance remain incomplete.

papers.title: Large Language Models Help Humans Verify Truthfulness -- Except When They Are Convincingly Wrong
papers.gap: Convincing wrong explanations can reduce human reliability, requiring explicit uncertainty and evidence-bound interaction design.

papers.title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
papers.gap: Efficient document grounding remains local to supplied context and does not resolve multi-source temporal conflict or graph state.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.gap: Retrieved passages improve generation but citations are not span-enforced and parametric/retrieved conflicts are unresolved.

papers.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
papers.gap: A static corpus and latent retrieval improve knowledge access without user-visible attribution or evidence acceptance state.

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.gap: Retrieval recall is a hard bottleneck and relevance scores do not imply entailment or evidence sufficiency.

papers.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
papers.gap: Efficient relevance ranking does not verify claims, calibrate acceptance, or preserve scientific relation provenance.

papers.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
papers.gap: Fusion over many passages can synthesize unsupported answers and offers no explicit source-conflict state.

papers.title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens
papers.gap: Massive retrieval is infrastructure-heavy, corpus-static, and not designed for auditable scientific evidence admission.

papers.title: PAQ: 65 Million Probably-Asked Questions and What You Can Do With Them
papers.gap: Generated question corpora inherit generator bias and do not supply scientific evidence sufficiency or contradiction labels.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.gap: Action traces improve inspectability but do not guarantee that observations support the final claim or that agents are independent.

papers.title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
papers.gap: Early reasoning errors steer later retrieval; there is no independent evidence sufficiency gate before synthesis.

papers.title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.gap: Token-level uncertainty is a heuristic trigger and repeated retrieval adds cost without structured conflict resolution.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.gap: Reflection tokens are produced by the same learned system, leaving correlated error and calibration risks.

papers.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
papers.gap: Recursive summaries can erase qualifiers and provenance; updates and contradiction-aware re-indexing remain open.

papers.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
papers.gap: Graph extraction errors propagate into retrieval and QA accuracy does not test evidence-state admission or temporal conflict.

papers.title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
papers.gap: Black-box mixtures improve utility but expose little claim-level attribution, calibration, or update provenance.

papers.title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
papers.gap: A learned complexity router can be brittle under distribution shift and does not model evidence disagreement.

papers.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
papers.gap: Benefits depend on tasks and agent diversity; shared-model correlated errors, cost, and external evidence remain unresolved.

papers.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
papers.gap: MAD is hyperparameter-sensitive and often fails to beat self-consistency, motivating selective rather than always-on debate.

papers.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
papers.gap: SOP-based role coordination targets software artifacts; message structure alone does not guarantee factual independence or evidence correctness.

papers.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
papers.gap: Persona specialization and emergent communication do not establish error independence or calibrated scientific adjudication.

papers.title: ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate
papers.gap: A debating evaluator can inherit model and persona bias; alignment to human judgments is not evidence-grounded truth calibration.

papers.title: ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus among Diverse LLMs
papers.gap: Diverse closed models and multi-round discussion are costly; confidence-weighted consensus still relies on self-reported certainty.

papers.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
papers.gap: The authors report judge fairness and stopping sensitivity; divergence is not equivalent to evidence correctness.

papers.title: Exchange-of-Thought: Enhancing Large Language Model Capabilities through Cross-Model Communication
papers.gap: Cross-model communication can share useful insights and shared mistakes; no provenance contract distinguishes them.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.gap: Verbal feedback is not an external truth signal and persistent memory can accumulate incorrect reflections.

papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.gap: Self-feedback shares the generator's blind spots and provides neither source diversity nor calibrated abstention.

papers.title: Removal of Hallucination on Hallucination: Debate-Augmented RAG
papers.gap: Debating both retrieval and generation raises cost and still needs tests against evidence pollution, correlated agents, and graph updates.

papers.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
papers.gap: Task success aggregates hide claim-level evidence quality, run drift, and intermediate coordination failure.

papers.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
papers.gap: Synthetic tool traces and changing APIs create reproducibility and execution-validity gaps beyond benchmark success.

papers.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
papers.gap: Software issue resolution does not transfer directly to scientific evidence quality; environment and benchmark drift remain material.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.gap: Believable social simulation is evaluated for plausibility, not scientific factuality, evidence sufficiency, or calibrated decisions.

papers.title: RotatE: Knowledge Graph Embedding by Relational Rotation in Complex Space
papers.gap: Static embedding patterns omit source text, uncertainty, and time-varying scientific truth.

papers.title: TuckER: Tensor Factorization for Knowledge Graph Completion
papers.gap: Static link completion scores are not evidence-calibrated and assume a fixed closed-world graph snapshot.

papers.title: KG-BERT: BERT for Knowledge Graph Completion
papers.gap: Triple classification underuses global graph structure and cannot show which document span justifies a prediction.

papers.title: Composition-based Multi-Relational Graph Convolutional Networks
papers.gap: Compositional message passing improves static completion but does not model provenance, supersession, or conflicting evidence.

papers.title: Tensor Decompositions for Temporal Knowledge Base Completion
papers.gap: Timestamped factorization captures temporal patterns but not textual evidence, event granularity, or causal supersession.

papers.title: TeMP: Temporal Message Passing for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
papers.gap: Temporal sparsity and frequency bias persist; transductive completion lacks document provenance and claim admission state.

papers.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting with Neural ODE
papers.gap: TANGO's continuous dynamics remain black-box and extrapolation quality does not establish source-backed scientific validity.

papers.title: xERTE: Explainable Reasoning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Forecasting Future Links
papers.gap: Attended subgraphs are useful explanations but are not causal proof or document-level evidence provenance.

papers.title: Search to Pass Messages for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
papers.gap: Search paths optimize benchmark completion and do not encode evidence sufficiency or conflict arbitration.

papers.title: Complex Evolutional Pattern Learning for Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
papers.gap: History-window patterns forecast facts without source-level evidence and remain sensitive to temporal benchmark artifacts.

papers.title: TimeTraveler: Reinforcement Learning for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting
papers.gap: Sparse-reward path search can cascade early errors and provides no scientific-document provenance contract.

papers.title: QA-GNN: Reasoning with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs for Question Answering
papers.gap: Performance depends on external KG completeness and does not expose graph-construction uncertainty or evidence spans.

papers.title: GreaseLM: Graph REASoning Enhanced Language Models for Question Answering
papers.gap: Latent graph-language fusion improves QA but intermediate claims are not directly auditable or selectively admitted.

papers.title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
papers.gap: The graph is largely given; extraction uncertainty, document provenance, and temporal graph maintenance remain outside scope.

papers.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.gap: Dual-level graph retrieval is efficient, but extraction/update consistency and calibrated relation admission are not solved.

papers.title: Deep Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: A predictive hidden state is difficult to interpret and does not prescribe evidence-grounded pedagogical interventions.

papers.title: Dynamic Key-Value Memory Networks for Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: Latent concept slots require response labels and do not connect mastery estimates to source evidence coverage.

papers.title: A Self-Attentive Model for Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: Sequence prediction depends on question-skill metadata and does not test whether generated feedback causes learning gains.

papers.title: Deep-IRT: Make Deep Learning Based Knowledge Tracing Explainable Using Item Response Theory
papers.gap: IRT-style interpretability is still response-centric and omits evidence provenance and intervention effectiveness.

papers.title: Context-Aware Attentive Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: Attention and Rasch components improve interpretability but attention is not causal mastery or evidence coverage.

papers.title: GIKT: A Graph-based Interaction Model for Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: Performance depends on a static concept-question graph whose provenance and update uncertainty are not modeled.

papers.title: RKT: Relation-Aware Self-Attention for Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: Exercise relations and forgetting improve prediction but not evidence-grounded feedback or causal personalization.

papers.title: SAINT+: Integrating Temporal Features for EdNet Correctness Prediction
papers.gap: Temporal response features optimize correctness prediction and do not validate resource recommendation or scientific comprehension.

papers.title: simpleKT: A Simple But Tough-to-Beat Baseline for Knowledge Tracing
papers.gap: A strong simple predictor exposes weak evaluation gains in prior KT work but still does not establish causal learning or evidence-grounded feedback.

papers.title: pyKT: A Python Library to Benchmark Deep Learning based Knowledge Tracing Models
papers.gap: Benchmark standardization does not provide gold outcomes for evidence-linked adaptive scientific tutoring.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
papers.gap: Capability tests are manually authored and can leave unanticipated evidence and temporal failure modes uncovered.

papers.title: Dynabench: Rethinking Benchmarking in NLP
papers.gap: Human-in-the-loop adversarial collection is costly and evolving rounds complicate longitudinal comparability.

papers.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
papers.gap: Retrieval relevance across domains does not measure generation support, evidence completeness, or graph correctness.

papers.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
papers.gap: Static multiple-choice accuracy is vulnerable to contamination and cannot diagnose evidence-grounded system behavior.

papers.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
papers.gap: Broad scenarios improve transparency but API drift and scenario selection do not yield scientific IE causal attribution.

papers.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
papers.gap: End-task completion does not isolate evidence calibration, provenance fidelity, or collaboration failure.

papers.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
papers.gap: Pairwise preference is not factuality, reproducibility, or scientific evidence quality and model pools drift over time.

papers.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.gap: LLM-judged metrics can vary by judge and prompt; reference-free scores need external calibration and audit trails.

papers.title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
papers.gap: Synthetic training examples and learned judges can bias scores; graph and agent-level causal effects remain hidden.

papers.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding
papers.gap: Static answer metrics test context length, not provenance-preserving extraction, conflict handling, or public experiment lineage.

papers.title: Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models
papers.gap: STORM optimizes sourced long-form writing, not scientific claim verification, graph state, or controlled experiments.

papers.title: Synthesizing scientific literature with retrieval-augmented language models
papers.gap: OpenScholar's strong literature synthesis does not expose a full entity-relation admission state machine, learner feedback, or temporal conflict layer.

papers.title: Language agents achieve superhuman synthesis of scientific knowledge
papers.gap: PaperQA2 targets scientific synthesis; corpus access and search quality remain bottlenecks and no persistent evidence-state learner loop is provided.

papers.title: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
papers.gap: Human-guided multi-agent science is validated in one costly biomedical setting; general evidence calibration and reproducible transfer remain open.

papers.title: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
papers.gap: Literature-graph idea generation cannot itself establish novelty or empirical validity and needs external search plus registered experiments.
